question: A 22-year-old woman took 30 paracetamol tablets 6 hours ago and currently feels completely well with normal vital signs. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.text: Measure serum paracetamol, plot on Rumack-Matthew nomogram, and start N-acetylcysteine if above the treatment line

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Asymptomatic presentation at 6 hours is characteristic of paracetamol overdose — NAPQI accumulation precedes hepatocellular necrosis by hours. The Rumack-Matthew nomogram at 4–12h post-ingestion guides NAC therapy. Early NAC (within 8–10 hours) is highly hepatoprotective.

answers.text: Reassure and discharge — no liver damage is possible since she is asymptomatic at 6 hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Dangerous error. Asymptomatic presentation at 6 hours is the RULE for paracetamol overdose, not a sign of safety. Hepatic necrosis develops at 24–72 hours. Discharging without measuring serum paracetamol could result in preventable liver failure.

answers.text: Give activated charcoal and observe for 4 hours before any further intervention

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. At 6 hours, activated charcoal has minimal benefit (most paracetamol already absorbed). Delaying the nomogram-guided decision by a further 4 hours risks missing the optimal NAC window (best within 8–10 hours of ingestion).

Incorrect at this stage. Transplant assessment is appropriate if established liver failure develops (24–72h). At 6 hours, the priority is nomogram-guided NAC therapy to PREVENT hepatotoxicity, not to manage established failure.

overallFeedback.feedback: The correct answer is measuring paracetamol level and using the Rumack-Matthew nomogram. Paracetamol overdose is deceptive — asymptomatic at 6h is expected, not reassuring. Liver failure develops at 24–72h. NAC is most effective within 8–10 hours of ingestion; never delay based on absence of symptoms.

Correct. Paracetamol overdose management: (1) Measure serum level at 4–12h post-ingestion; (2) Plot on Rumack-Matthew nomogram; (3) If above treatment line, start NAC immediately. Early NAC prevents NAPQI-mediated hepatocellular necrosis.
